summary:
Astral Horizon is a web app that plans safe journeys across Mars for astronauts on foot or in a crew rover. Users pick any region on a 3D globe and the app loads NASA’s MOLA elevation data for it. They place a start and a destination, and it calculates three routes: the shortest, the safest and the most efficient.
For each route, Astral Horizon uses published physiology and vehicle models to estimate travel time, energy, oxygen and battery use, and the point of no return. It also suggests what equipment to bring. Crews can rehearse the route as a 3D hologram, ride it in first person, look around real NASA rover panoramas, and ask ASTRA, an offline AI navigator, for help. Everything works without internet, as it would have to on Mars.

details:
Astral Horizon is a traverse planner for Mars. Before an astronaut walks, or a crew rover drives, across the surface, it answers three questions: which way is safe, how long it will take, and whether the oxygen and battery will last the trip back.

You pick any region of Mars on a 3D globe or an atlas. The app loads NASA’s elevation data for that area. You place a start and a destination, and Astral Horizon calculates three routes: the shortest, the safest (gentlest slopes) and the most efficient (least energy). For each route it estimates time, climb, energy, oxygen use or battery use, and a “point of no return”: the farthest point you can reach and still get home safely. It also builds a packing list for the trip.

The plan can then be explored in several ways:

  • 3D hologram: the terrain and the route, plus the suit, the rover and each piece of equipment.
  • First-person ride: a drive along the route from the rover’s camera.
  • Real Mars panoramas: a look around 360° images taken by NASA’s rovers.
  • ASTRA: an offline navigator that answers questions about the mission.

How it works
The terrain is NASA Mars Global Surveyor MOLA elevation data from NASA’s Planetary Data System. Routes are found with Dijkstra’s shortest-path algorithm over the elevation grid. Ground steeper than the safe limit is treated as impassable. Walking energy follows the Santee et al. (2001) load-carriage model, adjusted for Mars gravity (3.71 m/s²), and walking speed on slopes follows Tobler’s hiking function. Oxygen use is calculated from energy spent: about 1 litre of O₂ per 20.1 kJ. Rover energy is based on rolling resistance, grade and drivetrain efficiency.

Benefits and intended impact
On Mars there is no rescue, so every excursion must be planned before anyone leaves the habitat. Astral Horizon turns raw elevation data into decisions crews and planners can act on: where to go, what to bring, and when to turn back. Because it works fully offline, it suits places with no internet, such as a Mars base, a remote field test or a classroom. It also makes mission planning visible and understandable for students and the public.

Tools and technologies

  • Frontend: React and Vite (JavaScript), with Canvas 2D and WebGL graphics.
  • Backend: Python with FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy and Pillow.
  • Deployment: Docker, GitHub, GitHub Actions and Coolify.
  • NASA data: MOLA elevation (PDS), NASA/JPL-Caltech rover panoramas and NASA Solar System Treks imagery.
  • Companion app: Rover Control, a separate app for driving our ARES rover prototype over Wi-Fi with live sensor data (battery, obstacle distance, ultrasonic sweep, compass).

How it’s creative
Earlier traverse planners, such as MIT’s SEXTANT research, were research prototypes. Astral Horizon brings the same idea to a web app anyone can open. It lets you plan anywhere on Mars from a 3D globe, rehearse the route in first person before committing, inspect every piece of equipment as a hologram, and ask an offline AI navigator for help, all in one interface.

Factors we considered

  • Safety first: the return trip, oxygen reserve and point of no return are part of every plan.
  • Accuracy and honesty: real NASA data where it exists, published models for estimates, and clear on-screen notes about limits. The global elevation map shows one height every 463 m, so small hazards are invisible, and oxygen and battery figures are estimates.
  • Offline use: all NASA data can be downloaded once with an offline pack.
  • Accessibility and performance: keyboard controls, readable layouts, and smooth graphics on ordinary laptops.
  • Ease of use: one-click start scripts for Mac and Windows.
